quick: 40 mg OD; up to 80 mg OD
Serum uric acid, LFTs, CV status
summary: Febuxostat is a xanthine oxidase inhibitor for chronic hyperuricemia in gout, used when allopurinol is inadequate, not tolerated or inadvisable. Started at 40 mg once daily, increased to 80 mg if target uric acid not reached. Carries a boxed warning for cardiovascular death.
indications: Chronic management of hyperuricemia in adults with gout inadequately controlled by, intolerant of, or unsuitable for allopurinol

dosage.d: Start 40 mg once daily; increase to 80 mg if sUA >=6 mg/dL after 2 weeks

admin: Take once daily, with or without food or antacids
Start concurrent NSAID or colchicine to prevent gout flares
Do not stop for a flare; treat the flare and continue febuxostat
Recheck serum uric acid 2 weeks after starting/dose change
Limit dose to 40 mg in severe renal impairment
moa: Selectively and potently inhibits both oxidized and reduced forms of xanthine oxidase, blocking conversion of hypoxanthine to xanthine and xanthine to uric acid. This lowers serum uric acid. Unlike allopurinol it does not inhibit other purine/pyrimidine enzymes at therapeutic doses.

relative: Established cardiovascular disease (CV death risk - boxed warning)

preg: Insufficient human data; avoid unless clearly needed. Animal studies showed no major effects but human safety is not established.
lact: Not recommended; presence in human milk unknown. Decide to discontinue nursing or drug considering importance to mother.
renal: No adjustment for mild-moderate impairment. In severe impairment (CrCl 15-29 mL/min) limit to 40 mg once daily. Not studied in CrCl <15 mL/min.
hepatic: No adjustment for mild-moderate impairment. Use with caution in severe hepatic impairment (not studied). Monitor LFTs.

major: Azathioprine / mercaptopurine / pegloticase analogues - contraindicated/avoid (xanthine oxidase metabolizes these, causing toxic accumulation)
moderate: Concurrent urate-lowering agents - generally avoid duplication
minor: Antacids - no significant effect on absorption
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food.
interactions.alcohol: Limit; alcohol raises uric acid and may precipitate flares.
interactions.diagnostics: Lowers serum uric acid; may transiently elevate liver enzymes.

monitoring: Serum uric acid 2 weeks after start and dose changes (target <6 mg/dL)
Liver function tests at baseline and periodically / if symptoms
counsel: Expect possible gout flares early; do not stop the drug
Seek care for chest pain, shortness of breath, weakness, slurred speech
Report dark urine, jaundice, severe rash or fatigue
Take once daily regardless of food
pk: Urate lowering within days; assess at 2 weeks
Store at 20-25 C, protect from light
pearls: Useful when allopurinol fails, is not tolerated, or is contraindicated
Boxed warning: higher CV death risk vs allopurinol (CARES trial)
Always co-prescribe flare prophylaxis at initiation
missed: Take the missed dose when remembered. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip it; do not double up.
overdose: No specific antidote; manage with supportive care and symptom-directed treatment. Hemodialysis is not an effective means of removal.
